intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of the 12th-century Khmer Empire. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for a full-day pass covering Angkor Wat, Bayon Temple, and Ta Prohm, the jungle-wrapped ruin made famous by Tomb Raider.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda Visit
experiences.description: Tour the stunning Royal Palace complex and the adjacent Silver Pagoda, home to a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles and a life-sized gold Buddha adorned with diamonds. Combine with a visit to the nearby National Museum to see the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine white-sand beaches of Koh Rong Samloem, one of Cambodia's most beautiful and relatively unspoiled islands. Swim in crystal-clear turquoise waters, snorkel around coral reefs, and experience bioluminescent plankton glowing in the sea after dark on a guided night swim.

experiences.name: Khmer Cooking Class and Phsar Leu Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Khmer cooking class led by a local chef, beginning with a guided walk through a bustling local market to select fresh ingredients like lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime. Learn to prepare traditional dishes such as Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and Khmer red curry, then enjoy your meal together.

experiences.name: Killing Fields and Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
experiences.description: Visit the deeply moving Choeung Ek Genocidal Center, the most significant of Cambodia's Killing Fields, followed by the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 prison) in the city. An essential and sobering cultural experience that provides profound insight into Cambodia's tragic recent history under the Khmer Rouge regime.
experiences.location: Choeung Ek and Tuol Sleng, Phnom Penh

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked budget taxi or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort layout.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or a local street food stall near the resort if available upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night — keep Day 1 light. Pre-book airport transfer in advance to save money (around $8–$15 USD for a shared shuttle). Confirm hotel night check-in policy before arrival. Exchange a small amount of USD or use an ATM at the airport for immediate expenses. Cambodia widely accepts USD.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a simple breakfast at the resort or a nearby local café. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront to get your bearings and enjoy the coastal scenery near the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach area on foot. Visit a nearby local market to pick up snacks, water, and essentials. Rent a bicycle ($2–$3/day) to explore the surrounding village and coastal road at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a beachside spot to watch the sunset — one of Cambodia's most underrated coastal experiences. Stroll along the beach strip and browse local restaurants for a relaxed first dinner in Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Simple breakfast at the resort café or a local bakery — rice porridge (bobor) or baguette with eggs ($1–$2)
meals.lunch: Local Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) from a street stall or small local restaurant ($1.50–$2.50)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled seafood at a beachside local eatery — grilled fish with rice and vegetables ($4–$6)

day_by_day.notes: November in Cambodia is post-rainy season — expect pleasant weather, lower humidity, and lush green landscapes. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen. Budget tip: eat where locals eat to save significantly on meals.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local Buddhist temple (wat) near the resort area. Dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees) as a sign of respect. Observe morning monk rituals if timed early (around 6–7 AM). Entrance is usually free or a small donation is appreciated.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk or local bus to explore the nearest town center. Visit a local fresh market (psar) to experience Cambodian daily life, sample tropical fruits, and browse handmade goods. Pick up affordable souvenirs like scarves (krama) for $2–$4.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or low-cost cultural show or simply dine at a local family-run restaurant. Try traditional Cambodian dishes and chat with locals to learn about the culture.

meals.breakfast: Rice with fried egg and cucumber at a local breakfast stall ($1–$1.50)
meals.lunch: Amok (traditional Cambodian fish curry in coconut milk) at a local restaurant ($2.50–$4)
meals.dinner: Lok lak (stir-fried beef with rice and lime-pepper sauce) at a budget Khmer restaurant ($3–$5)

day_by_day.notes: Always negotiate tuk-tuk fares before getting in — typical short rides cost $1–$3. Carry small USD bills for ease of payment. Respect temple etiquette: remove shoes before entering, speak quietly, and avoid pointing feet toward altars.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip preparation: take an early morning bus or shared minivan toward Sihanoukville or a nearby historical/cultural town (depending on resort location). Explore the town's waterfront promenade and colonial-era architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local history or cultural museum in the nearest town. Many provincial museums in Cambodia have free or very low-cost entry ($1–$2). Learn about Khmer history, the Angkor Empire, and local traditions through exhibits and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by early evening. Relax on the beach and enjoy the cooler evening air. Visit a local night market (if available) for street food and shopping.

meals.breakfast: Nom banh chok (Khmer noodles with green fish curry) from a morning street vendor ($1–$1.50)
meals.lunch: Baguette sandwich with pâté or grilled pork from a local bakery stall ($1–$2) — a French colonial culinary legacy
meals.dinner: Grilled corn, skewers, and fried rice from night market stalls ($3–$5 total)

day_by_day.notes: Shared minivans are the most budget-friendly way to travel between towns ($3–$8 depending on distance). Book through your guesthouse or a local travel agent the evening before. Keep a copy of your passport for any bus bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day — spend the morning swimming, snorkeling, or simply relaxing on the beach near the resort. Rent basic snorkel gear from a local beach shack ($3–$5/hour) to explore shallow reef areas if available nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget boat tour to nearby islands (if available from the resort's coastal area). Many group boat tours to local islands cost $10–$15 and include snorkeling stops. Alternatively, kayak along the coastline ($3–$5/hour rental).
day_by_day.evening: Beach bonfire or sunset happy hour at a local beach bar. Many budget beach bars offer $1 draft beers or $1.50 cocktails during happy hour. Watch the stars from the beach — coastal Cambodia offers stunning night skies.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie bowl or fresh tropical fruit plate from a beach café ($2–$3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local market or beachside BBQ — grilled squid on a stick ($0.50–$1 each)
meals.dinner: Seafood barbecue platter (prawns, crab, fish) at a beachside local restaurant ($5–$8)

day_by_day.notes: Always check water conditions before swimming — November seas are generally calm on Cambodia's southern coast. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect marine ecosystems. Bargain politely for boat tours and water activity rentals.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby historical or archaeological site. If near the coast, explore local Khmer ruins, ancient pagodas, or hilltop temples accessible by tuk-tuk or rented motorbike. Hire a local guide for deeper historical insight ($5–$10 for a half-day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the historical site or visit a nearby village for a community-based cultural experience. Many villages welcome visitors and offer insight into traditional Cambodian crafts like weaving, pottery, or fishing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Visit a local cooking class or food demonstration if available in the area ($10–$15 for a budget class) — learn to cook Khmer staples like amok or papaya salad.

meals.breakfast: Congee (rice porridge) with dried fish and pickled vegetables at a local breakfast shop ($1–$1.50)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch from a local market — sticky rice parcels, fresh spring rolls, and fruit ($2–$3)
meals.dinner: Home-cooked Khmer meal if attending a cooking class, or dine at a local family restaurant ($3–$5)

day_by_day.notes: Renting a motorbike ($5–$8/day) gives maximum flexibility for exploring rural areas but ensure you have an international driver's license and always wear a helmet. Alternatively, negotiate a full-day tuk-tuk rate ($10–$15) for guided exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local Buddhist pagoda for morning prayers and meditation. Many pagodas allow respectful visitors to observe or even briefly participate in morning chanting. Explore the pagoda grounds, stupas, and religious artwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore local handicraft markets or artisan workshops. Look for hand-woven silk scarves (krama), silver jewelry, and traditional Khmer artwork. Practice your bargaining skills — always smile and be respectful. Budget $5–$15 for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free traditional Apsara dance performance if available at a nearby cultural center or restaurant. Alternatively, explore a local night market and enjoy street food while mingling with locals and fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: French-style baguette with butter and coffee (café noir) at a local café ($1.50–$2)
meals.lunch: Khmer red curry with jasmine rice at a local restaurant ($2.50–$3.50)
meals.dinner: Barbecue mixed platter (pork, chicken, vegetables) at a local grill restaurant with communal seating ($4–$6)

day_by_day.notes: Apsara dance is a UNESCO-recognized art form and central to Khmer cultural identity — a truly memorable experience. Check local notice boards or ask your hotel about free cultural events. Tip performers if you enjoy the show.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach walk or yoga session on the beach (many resorts or beach cafés offer free or low-cost morning yoga, $3–$5). Reflect on the trip so far and plan any last-minute activities or purchases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a full afternoon to explore a different stretch of the coastline. Walk or cycle to a quieter, less touristy beach section for a more authentic experience. Collect shells, read a book, or simply enjoy the tranquility.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local spa for a traditional Khmer massage — budget options start at $6–$10/hour for a full-body massage. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort or a nearby beach lounge.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancake with honey and fresh fruit from a beach café ($2–$3) — a Southeast Asian backpacker classic
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut ($1) and papaya salad (bok lahong) from a street vendor ($1.50–$2)
meals.dinner: Whole grilled snapper with steamed rice and morning glory stir-fry at a local seafood shack ($5–$7)

day_by_day.notes: Traditional Khmer massage (chhmob) uses pressure point techniques and herbal compresses. Always choose licensed massage establishments. November weather is ideal for outdoor activities — enjoy the pleasant temperatures before they rise.

day_by_day.morning: Final cultural exploration — visit any remaining local sites, temples, or viewpoints you haven't yet seen. Consider climbing a nearby hill or viewpoint for panoramic coastal views. Many such spots are free or charge a minimal fee ($0.50–$1).
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and last-minute market browsing. Stock up on Cambodian coffee (a local specialty), spices, silk products, and handcrafted goods to bring home. Visit a local social enterprise shop where purchases support local artisans and communities.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you've discovered during your trip. Treat yourself to a slightly more elaborate Cambodian meal — try a tasting menu of multiple Khmer dishes to celebrate the journey.

meals.breakfast: Eggs benedict or local egg dish with fresh juice at a beach café ($3–$4)
meals.lunch: Banh mi sandwich with iced coffee ($2–$3) — quick and delicious while shopping
meals.dinner: Celebratory Khmer feast: amok, lok lak, green mango salad, and sticky rice with mango dessert at a top-rated local restaurant ($8–$12 for a generous spread)

day_by_day.notes: Pack purchased items carefully — Cambodian silk and ceramics require gentle handling. Declare any items over customs limits when returning home. Keep receipts for any significant purchases. Begin packing and organizing belongings for departure.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise on the beach — a peaceful and memorable way to say goodbye to Cambodia. Take photos, journal your memories, and soak in the last moments of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout is usually 11 AM — confirm with the hotel). Store luggage at the hotel if your departure is later. Take a final tuk-tuk ride through the local area for one last glimpse of Cambodian life.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport with ample time before your flight. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before departure for international flights. Use remaining local currency on airport snacks or last-minute duty-free gifts.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast — rice soup or noodles at a local stall near the resort ($1.50–$2)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a nearby café before departure ($3–$5)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on-board flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: A 10-day budget trip to Cambodia can be done comfortably for $30–$50 USD per day including accommodation, meals, transport, and activities. Always keep emergency cash separate from your main wallet. Leave a positive review for local businesses that provided great service — it supports the local economy. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh or Siem Reap International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Grab a light snack from the hotel if available.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day only. Keep luggage accessible for easy check-in. Exchange some currency (USD is widely accepted in Cambodia) at the airport. Rest well for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow walk along the beachfront to get acquainted with the surroundings and enjoy the coastal scenery near the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby local village or town on foot or by tuk-tuk. Visit a local market to sample fresh tropical fruits and get a feel for Cambodian daily life. Browse handmade crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area for a sunset stroll along the beach. Dine at a beachside restaurant and enjoy fresh seafood while watching the sunset over the Gulf of Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Street food or local eatery at the nearby market - try Lok Lak (stir-fried beef) or fresh spring rolls (~$5-8)
meals.dinner: Beachside seafood restaurant near the resort - grilled fish, prawns, and rice (~$12-18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today to recover from jet lag. November is generally a pleasant time in coastal Cambodia with lower humidity. Carry insect repellent and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning boat trip or kayaking excursion along the coastline. Explore nearby islands or mangroves if accessible from the resort area. Enjoy the calm morning waters and scenic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fishing village to learn about traditional Cambodian coastal life and fishing techniques. Interact with locals and observe how fishing boats are crafted and maintained.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a night market or local food street in the nearest town. Sample Cambodian street food including Nom Banh Chok (Khmer noodles) and fresh coconut desserts.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort - tropical fruit platter and Cambodian rice porridge (Bobor)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at the fishing village - grilled squid and steamed crab (~$8-12)
meals.dinner: Night market street food experience - variety of small dishes and snacks (~$6-10)

day_by_day.notes: Bring waterproof bags for the morning boat trip. Wear comfortable sandals for the fishing village walk. Bargaining is acceptable and expected at local markets.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby historic temple or pagoda. Cambodia's coastal regions have several ancient Khmer-influenced temples and Buddhist pagodas worth visiting. Hire a local guide for cultural context and historical insights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the temple complex or visit a second nearby pagoda. Learn about Theravada Buddhism, observe monks in their daily routines, and admire intricate stone carvings and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage at a local spa or wellness center to relax after a day of exploration.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Restaurant near the temple site - Amok (fish curry in coconut milk) and steamed rice (~$7-10)
meals.dinner: Mid-range Khmer restaurant in town - try Samlor Machu (sour soup) and beef skewers (~$10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples - cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes before entering temple buildings. A local tuk-tuk driver can serve as an affordable guide (~$15-20 for the day).

day_by_day.morning: Beach day - relax on the pristine beachfront near the resort. Try water sports such as snorkeling, paddleboarding, or jet skiing offered by local vendors on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling trip to a nearby coral reef or island (if available from the resort location). Explore the underwater marine life of the Gulf of Thailand with rented gear or a guided tour.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort bar or a nearby beach bar. Enjoy a relaxed evening with live acoustic music if available.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort - eggs, toast, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Beach shack lunch - fresh coconut, grilled corn, and seafood skewers (~$5-8)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner - set menu with Khmer specialties and fresh catch of the day (~$15-20)

day_by_day.notes: Apply high SPF sunscreen regularly. Stay hydrated throughout the day. Book water sports and snorkeling tours in advance through the resort concierge for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Travel inland or to a nearby city for a cultural immersion day. Visit a local Cambodian museum or cultural center to learn about Khmer history, art, and traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a traditional Cambodian village. Participate in a cooking class where you learn to prepare authentic Khmer dishes using local ingredients and traditional methods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance or cultural show if available in the area. This classical Khmer dance form is a UNESCO-recognized intangible cultural heritage.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departing
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class (~$15-25 including class fee)
meals.dinner: Restaurant attached to the cultural performance venue - traditional Khmer set dinner (~$12-18)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and cultural performance in advance. Photography may be restricted inside museums - always ask permission. Bring a light jacket for air-conditioned venues.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a local Buddhist temple for the almsgiving ceremony (if accessible). Watch monks collect morning offerings from devotees - a deeply spiritual and photogenic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby colonial-era town or heritage district. Walk through French colonial architecture, old shophouses, and historical buildings that reflect Cambodia's layered past.
day_by_day.evening: Riverside dining experience if near a river town. Enjoy a boat dinner cruise or dine at a riverside restaurant with views of the water and city lights.

meals.breakfast: Local Cambodian breakfast near the temple - rice porridge with dried fish and tea (~$3-5)
meals.lunch: Heritage district café - sandwiches, salads, and Cambodian fusion dishes (~$8-12)
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant - fresh river prawns, grilled fish, and Khmer curry (~$12-18)

day_by_day.notes: Be respectful and quiet during the almsgiving ceremony. Do not touch monks or hand offerings directly. The colonial architecture areas make for excellent photography in the golden morning light.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Siem Reap (if not already based there) to visit the iconic Angkor Wat temple complex. Arrive early to beat the crowds and witness the sunrise over the ancient temple spires.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Angkor Archaeological Park - visit Bayon Temple with its famous stone faces and Ta Prohm temple where tree roots engulf ancient ruins. Hire an official licensed guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to base accommodation. Enjoy a well-deserved rest and dinner after a full day of temple exploration.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed breakfast or early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Restaurant within the Angkor Park area - Khmer buffet or à la carte (~$10-15)
meals.dinner: Casual restaurant near the resort - noodle soup or fried rice (~$7-12)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Angkor Wat pass in advance (1-day pass ~$37 USD). Wear comfortable walking shoes - you will cover significant ground. Carry plenty of water and a hat. This is a UNESCO World Heritage Site - treat it with respect.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning - take a sunrise walk along the beach, collect shells, and soak in the last moments of the coastal scenery. Consider a final swim or snorkel session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit local artisan workshops or silk weaving centers to learn about traditional Cambodian craftsmanship. Purchase authentic handmade souvenirs such as silk scarves, lacquerware, or silver jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best restaurant in the area. Celebrate the trip with a special Cambodian feast including all your favorite dishes discovered during the journey.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort - full spread to enjoy one last time
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café near the artisan workshops (~$6-10)
meals.dinner: Upscale Khmer restaurant for a farewell dinner - tasting menu with Amok, Lok Lak, and traditional desserts (~$20-30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing in the evening. Confirm flight details and arrange airport transfer through the resort. Keep souvenirs within airline carry-on or checked baggage limits.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a last breakfast and check out of the hotel. Take a final walk along the beachfront and capture last photos of the beautiful Cambodian coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to the airport. Arrive at least 2-3 hours before your departure flight. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts. Reflect on the incredible 10-day Cambodian adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cambodia with wonderful memories of ancient temples, vibrant culture, pristine beaches, and warm Khmer hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort before checkout
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café - light meal before the flight (~$8-15)
meals.dinner: On-flight meal or at layover destination

day_by_day.notes: Keep travel documents, passports, and boarding passes easily accessible. Cambodia does not require an exit tax for most travelers but confirm with your airline. Ensure all souvenirs comply with customs regulations - avoid purchasing items made from protected wildlife or ancient artifacts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh or Siem Reap International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort awaits you with a personal concierge. Enjoy a chilled welcome drink and fresh towels in your air-conditioned vehicle. Check in to your Beachfront suite and unwind with a complimentary late-night amenity tray prepared by the resort.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night in-suite dining: charcuterie board, Cambodian spring rolls, fresh tropical fruit platter, and a bottle of Champagne arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: All activities begin Day 2 onward. Confirm private airport transfer with resort concierge 48 hours before landing. Luggage handling and express check-in are pre-arranged for a seamless arrival experience.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. Begin the day with a private sunrise yoga session on your beachfront terrace led by the resort's in-house wellness instructor. Follow with a full à la carte breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant overlooking the Gulf of Thailand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a private guided orientation tour of the surrounding coastal area. Explore the local fishing village by tuk-tuk, interact with artisan vendors, and visit a nearby Buddhist temple adorned with intricate Khmer carvings. Return to the resort for a 90-minute traditional Khmer massage at the luxury spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's overwater bar. Enjoy a private beachfront dinner under the stars with a curated 5-course Cambodian tasting menu prepared by the executive chef, featuring fresh-caught seafood and locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort oceanfront restaurant — eggs Benedict, tropical fruit bowl, Cambodian rice porridge (Bobor), freshly squeezed juices, and Kampot pepper-infused Bloody Mary
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — grilled tiger prawns, green mango salad, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Private beachfront 5-course tasting menu — amuse-bouche, Cambodian fish amok, grilled lobster with lemongrass butter, mango sorbet, and dark chocolate lava cake

day_by_day.notes: Book the Khmer massage at the spa in advance through the concierge. The beachfront dinner setup requires at least 4 hours' notice. November weather in coastal Cambodia is typically warm and dry — ideal beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat excursion to a secluded nearby island. Snorkel in crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and coral reefs. Your personal boat crew will pack a premium picnic hamper with Champagne, fresh sashimi, and Cambodian snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and enjoy free time at the infinity pool. Optional: private paddleboarding or kayaking session arranged by the resort's water sports team. Late afternoon visit to a nearby coastal mangrove forest via private longtail boat for a guided eco-tour.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Dress smart-casual for an elevated Cambodian-French fusion menu with an expertly curated wine list. Finish the evening with a bonfire on the private beach with signature cocktails.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast service — croissants, Cambodian rice cake (Num Ansom), fresh papaya, cold brew coffee, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Island picnic hamper — smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, fresh baguette, tropical fruit, and Moët & Chandon Champagne
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — foie gras with tamarind glaze, pan-seared barramundi with Khmer herb crust, and passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Speedboat excursion should be booked the previous evening. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and snorkeling gear (provided by resort). Mangrove eco-tour is best done at dusk for wildlife sightings including kingfishers and monitor lizards.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to Siem Reap (approximately 6–7 hours by road or 1 hour by domestic flight — recommend private charter flight for premium experience). Depart early to maximize time. Upon arrival, check in to a pre-arranged luxury property (resort concierge to coordinate) or use as a day-trip base.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the legendary Angkor Thom complex, including the Bayon Temple with its iconic 216 serene stone faces, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Your expert Khmer historian guide provides deep cultural and historical context unavailable on standard tours.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive sunset access to Phnom Bakheng hilltop temple (VIP permit arranged by concierge) for panoramic views over the Angkor jungle canopy. Dinner at one of Siem Reap's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — Cambodian Kuy Teav noodle soup, fresh fruit, and strong Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Private lunch at a curated garden restaurant near Angkor — amok curry, fresh spring rolls, and coconut desserts
meals.dinner: Malis Restaurant, Siem Reap — acclaimed modern Cambodian cuisine; try the slow-cooked beef lok lak and banana blossom salad

day_by_day.notes: Private charter flight from the nearest airport to Siem Reap is highly recommended for comfort and time efficiency. VIP Angkor Thom access and Phnom Bakheng sunset permit must be arranged at least 3 days in advance through a licensed tour operator. Dress modestly for temple visits — shoulders and knees covered.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private transfer to Angkor Wat for an exclusive sunrise viewing. Watch the sun rise behind the iconic five towers reflected in the lotus ponds — one of the world's most breathtaking spectacles. Private historian guide leads an in-depth 3-hour exploration of the bas-relief galleries depicting Hindu mythology and Khmer history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the mystical Ta Prohm temple, famously engulfed by ancient silk-cotton tree roots. Continue to the exquisitely detailed Banteay Srei temple, known as the 'Citadel of Women,' carved in pink sandstone. Private air-conditioned vehicle and guide throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Apsara dance performance dinner at a prestigious Siem Reap venue — watch UNESCO-recognized classical Khmer dance while enjoying a royal Cambodian banquet. Return to resort or overnight accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn packed breakfast box — croissants, boiled eggs, fresh fruit, and thermos of Cambodian coffee provided by hotel before sunrise departure
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the Angkor Archaeological Park — gourmet sandwiches, tropical fruit, chilled coconut water, and petit fours
meals.dinner: Apsara dance dinner at La Résidence d'Angkor or Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor — royal Khmer banquet with amok, lok lak, and Cambodian desserts

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise at Angkor Wat requires a 4:30 AM departure. This is an unmissable highlight — book the private guide and vehicle the night before. Angkor Archaeological Park pass (3-day pass recommended) must be purchased in advance. Stay hydrated throughout the day as November can still be warm.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for a curated, air-conditioned deep-dive into Khmer civilization, art, and the history of the Angkor Empire. Private guided tour with a museum scholar. Afterward, explore the Old French Quarter of Siem Reap on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Authentic Khmer cooking class at a luxury culinary school — learn to prepare traditional dishes like fish amok, green mango salad, and Cambodian banana cake using ingredients sourced from the local market. Optional: private tuk-tuk market tour preceding the class.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (private charter or road transfer). Arrive in time for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a private couples' or solo in-suite spa treatment — hot stone massage with Cambodian herbal compresses.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Siem Reap — French pastries, tropical fruit, eggs to order, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during your own cooking class — a truly personal and memorable lunch experience
meals.dinner: In-suite fine dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — personally curated menu by the executive chef upon return, with a welcome-back Champagne toast

day_by_day.notes: Coordinate return transfer timing with the resort concierge to ensure smooth logistics. The cooking class is a highlight for culture enthusiasts — book with Cuisine Wat Damnak or a comparable premium culinary school in Siem Reap. Confirm spa appointment upon return.

day_by_day.morning: Full relaxation day at Aegean Bliss Resort. Morning meditation and breathwork session on the beach led by the resort's wellness coach. Follow with a slow breakfast and a long swim in the warm Gulf waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat trip to a nearby uninhabited island for exclusive beach time. Snorkel, sunbathe, and enjoy a lavish Champagne and seafood picnic on a pristine white sand beach with no other tourists. Resort staff set up a shaded cabana, sun loungers, and a full picnic spread.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a sunset cocktail hour at the overwater bar. Attend an optional private cultural presentation by a local Khmer artist or historian arranged by the resort. Dinner at the resort's beachfront grill.

meals.breakfast: Beachfront breakfast at the resort — smoked salmon bagel, acai bowl, Cambodian sticky rice with mango, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Private island picnic — grilled lobster, king prawns, artisan bread, tropical fruit, and Moët & Chandon Rosé
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront grill — whole grilled red snapper, Cambodian-style grilled corn, and coconut sticky rice dessert

day_by_day.notes: The private island excursion is weather-dependent — confirm with the resort the morning of. This is an ideal day to recharge before the Phnom Penh cultural excursion. Request the resort's private cultural presentation at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer or domestic charter flight to Phnom Penh, Cambodia's vibrant capital. Check in to a pre-arranged luxury hotel (Four Seasons Phnom Penh recommended) or use as a day excursion. Begin with a private guided tour of the magnificent Royal Palace complex and the sacred Silver Pagoda, home to a life-size solid gold Buddha encrusted with 9,584 diamonds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sobering but essential visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and Choeung Ek Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant experience that provides crucial context to modern Cambodia. Private expert guide provides sensitive, informed commentary.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise along the Tonlé Sap and Mekong Rivers aboard a private luxury riverboat. Enjoy Champagne and canapés as the golden light reflects off the water and the Phnom Penh skyline glows at dusk. Dinner at one of Phnom Penh's top fine-dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — Cambodian Num Pang sandwich, fresh fruit, and iced coffee
meals.lunch: Rooftop lunch in Phnom Penh — Khmer beef salad, amok curry, and fresh coconut at a premium riverside restaurant
meals.dinner: Malis Phnom Penh or Topaz Restaurant — refined Cambodian or French-Cambodian fusion; try the Kampot pepper crab and mango sticky rice

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visit is emotionally intense — allow time for reflection. Photography is permitted in some areas but always with respect. Dress conservatively for the Royal Palace. Private riverboat sunset cruise must be booked in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Morning exploration of Phnom Penh's vibrant riverside promenade and the renowned Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) — browse for premium silk scarves, Khmer silver jewelry, and handcrafted lacquerware as luxury souvenirs. Private guide assists with authentication and negotiation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia, home to the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture dating back to the 4th century. Private curator-led tour provides exclusive insight. Afterward, visit a renowned silk weaving workshop to witness traditional Cambodian textile artistry firsthand.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the resort bar with the resort manager. Indulge in a grand farewell dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — a chef's table experience with a personalized menu celebrating the flavors of Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Four Seasons Phnom Penh breakfast — full buffet with live cooking stations, Cambodian and international options, fresh pastries, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Phnom Penh restaurant near the National Museum — Khmer fish curry, grilled eggplant with shrimp paste, and fresh lime dessert
meals.dinner: Chef's table farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — 7-course personalized Cambodian tasting menu with wine pairing, prepared tableside by the executive chef

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours at the Russian Market for a thorough browse. The silk weaving workshop visit supports local artisans — purchases made here directly benefit the community. The chef's table experience at the resort must be reserved at least 48 hours in advance and is subject to availability.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the private beach. Optional: early morning snorkeling session or a final yoga class on the beach. Enjoy a long, indulgent farewell breakfast at the oceanfront restaurant.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout arranged by the resort (confirm with concierge). Spend remaining hours at the spa for a final relaxation treatment — aromatherapy facial and foot massage. Collect any last-minute artisan gifts from the resort boutique. Private luxury transfer to the airport departs in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cambodia with extraordinary memories. Private airport lounge access arranged by the resort concierge. Complimentary resort gift bag with Cambodian specialty coffee, Kampot pepper, and handcrafted silk keepsakes to take home.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full à la carte menu; eggs royale, Cambodian Kuy Teav noodle soup, tropical fruit platter, and freshly brewed Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort pool bar — club sandwich, green papaya salad, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium dining on departure

day_by_day.notes: Confirm late checkout (typically 2:00–4:00 PM for luxury guests) with the front desk the evening before. Ensure all valuables, passports, and travel documents are packed the night before. The resort concierge will arrange all departure logistics including luggage handling, airport transfer, and lounge access coordination.
